\subsection{Cross-species genome-wide associations with WorldClim PC1 identify shared orthologous genes across all species}

We performed GWAS in Arabidopsis, barley, rice, maize, and sorghum using a mixed linear model and kinship correction in GEMMA. Under Bonferroni correction, the number of significant SNPs was heterogeneous across species (Arabidopsis 30, rice 592, sorghum 6, barley 8, maize 1). To evaluate cross-species convergence beyond the Bonferroni tail, we selected the top 0.5\% of SNPs per species and mapped nearby genes to orthogroups. This yielded 20,762 Arabidopsis genes, 31,149 rice genes, 3,834 maize genes, 1,287 barley genes, and 1,274 sorghum genes.

Orthogroup integration identified 43,449 total orthogroups, with 17 orthogroups represented in all five species. Table~\ref{tab:shared_function_candidates_PC1} summarizes these shared orthogroups and reports, for each species, the strongest gene-level signal within each orthogroup as $-\log_{10}(P)$. As in the soil-N analysis, most associations remained species-specific, while a smaller subset of ortholog groups showed repeated signals across all taxa.
